summary: Independent review of p02/ch01 units 1-43: 10 errors, 48 minor. Main errors: u20 misplaced printed space (pravṛtter upalabdhir na), u21 Hindi drops the unclear word, u8 unmarked conjecture (kukṣisthaḥ), u3 Hindi ataḥ, u5 Hindi added/duplicated verb, u10 Hindi saṃprahana, u12/u15 unhedged probable identifications, u28/u40 Hindi रेत. Many minor: unstated-noun gram genders, missing Hindi glosses of doctrinal terms, iti/or consistency. GROUPING: 23-24 one statement; 25-26; 28-37 one run; 19-21 one argument; 42-43. No identification judged wrong, only unhedged. Human decisions: u15, u8, u21, u30, u5, u12.
glossary_suggestions: A misplaced printed space can move a final r, m or visarga to the start of the next token (u5 aniṃdyā maniṃdyena; u12 vātadevā sṛgdaram; u20 pravṛtte rupalabdhirna = pravṛtter upalabdhir na). Check this before proposing a stray-letter typo.
A dvandva takes the gender of its last member (vāta-pitta n.; pitta-śleṣman m.); but adjectives for an unstated noun carry no gender in gram (u14, 15, 18, 29-37).
Hindi retas = रेतस् यानी वीर्य (bare रेत means sand). Hindi सन्निपात needs the gloss तीनों दोषों का एक साथ होना.
Hindi saṃprahana = संप्रहन (not संप्रहनन); Hindi kalā needs 'झिल्लीदार परत'; ojas = ओज यानी जीवन-सार; bṛṃhaṇa = बृंहण यानी पुष्टि करने वाला.
asṛgdara, pradara: masculine nouns; probable identifications must be hedged ('probably') in both translations; garbhakoṣṭha = probably the womb; vātodara = probably abdominal swelling from Vāta.
Age bounds written as one compound (ūna-X ... atīta-Y) are rendered 'or' in both languages and both sexes (u23, u24).
Absolutives of caus. verbs (upasnehya, saṃśodhya) are active: 'having oleated / cleansed (them)'.
Open for the owner: u15 garbhaiva (case/alternatives), u8 śukrārtavahati, u21 prāptaviśarāḥ, u30 dahadviṣa, u5 mṛdumarogā- parse, u12 whether 'names' governs all four accusatives.
